shots.name: without-and-with-the-guard
shots.label: The same scripted attack, without the guard and with it
shots.note: Scenario a02: a web page tells the agent to POST .env. The replay sends real Claude Code hook payloads through the adapter. Without the guard three canary secrets leave; with it the upload is denied.

shots.name: real-claude-code-session
shots.label: A real Claude Code session: the hook denies the upload and the model reports it
shots.note: Not scripted. Claude Code 2.1.325 (headless) read a vendored file with a hidden instruction, read .env, tried the command, and was denied by the PreToolUse hook. Below the timeline is what the model told the user. The recorded store is examples/claude-code-session/graph.rl.
shots.command: TAINTTRAIL_DB=examples/claude-code-session/graph.rl {python} -m tainttrail log && echo && echo "Claude's reply to the user:" && echo && fold -s -w 104 examples/claude-code-session/claude-answer.txt

shots.name: attack-path
shots.label: The blocked call, its attack path, and the Cypher query that found it
shots.note: Rule TT001 on the real session. The path runs from the untrusted file to the host it named, to the call, to the sensitive file the call would upload. The query is stored on the finding and can be re-run against the store.

shots.name: viewer-overview
shots.label: The same graph in the browser, on Relate's WebAssembly build
shots.note: tainttrail ui serves a static viewer on 127.0.0.1. The recorded session is loaded into an in-memory Relate store in the page; every number on screen is the result of a Cypher query run there. Nothing leaves the machine.

shots.name: viewer-attack-path
shots.label: The blocked call as a path, with the query that found it run again in the page
shots.note: Rule TT001 on the real session. The stored Cypher query was run in the browser with the Run button; the nodes and relationships it returned are the ones highlighted in the diagram.

shots.name: viewer-timeline
shots.label: Session timeline: what each call touched and what it brought into the context
shots.note: The real session, call by call. Untrusted and sensitive content are marked where they entered; the denied call shows the destination only untrusted content named and the file it would have uploaded.

shots.name: viewer-console
shots.label: Read-only Cypher console in the browser
shots.note: Any read query against the recorded graph, run on Relate WASM. Here: every destination that only untrusted content named, and the calls that tried to send there.

shots.name: capability-scan
shots.label: Before anything runs: what the agent is configured with
shots.note: tainttrail scan reads agent configuration into the same graph: MCP servers, their tools with capability labels, permission rules, credential names. This is the sample setup in examples/agent-config (four MCP servers for Claude Code, two for Cursor).

shots.name: toxic-paths-and-fix
shots.label: Toxic tool combinations, and the smallest change that breaks them
shots.note: A toxic path is a source of untrusted text, a tool that reads private data and a way out, on one agent. fix searches for the cheapest set of permission changes that leaves no path open, and checks it by applying the change inside a Relate transaction, re-running the path query and rolling back.
shots.setup: rm -f {tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl* && TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail scan --path examples/agent-config/project --home examples/agent-config/home >/dev/null
shots.command: TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail paths --groups 6 --limit 2 && echo && TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail fix

shots.name: viewer-capability-map
shots.label: Capability map: servers, tools, what each can do, and the toxic paths between them
shots.note: The sample configuration of shot 08 in the viewer. Counts are computed in the page by the same path query the command line uses.
shots.setup: rm -rf {tmp}/tt-shot-ui-map {tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl* && TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail scan --path examples/agent-config/project --home examples/agent-config/home >/dev/null && TAINTTRAIL_DB={tmp}/tt-shot-agent-config.rl TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail ui --export-dir {tmp}/tt-shot-ui-map >/dev/null

shots.name: scenario-matrix
shots.label: The whole suite: 161 replayed scenarios
shots.note: 17 attacks modelled on public incident reports, 64 attack variants written by two reviewers against the edges of the rules, 10 ordinary workflows, 64 ordinary sessions written to find false alarms (32 were interrupted before the fixes), 3 harder cases, and 3 known gaps that are not stopped yet and stay in the suite. Every secret is a canary and every host is reserved; replay contacts nothing.

shots.name: doctor
shots.label: Installation check and measured hook latency
shots.command: cd {tmp} && rm -rf tt-shot-doctor && mkdir tt-shot-doctor && cd tt-shot-doctor && git init -q . && TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail init >/dev/null && TAINTTRAIL_KEY=screenshots-fixed-key {python} -m tainttrail doctor | sed -e 's#{root}#<repo>#g' -e 's#/tmp/[^ ]*tt-shot-doctor#<project>#g'
